desc: GitHub #60 and the audience's throw: the menu layer's places for a controller's own presses (TTYD_MENU_LAYER_TEST, the layer's own function on the bindings the cases name; a test's scripted presses are never moved, so no plugged-in controller is needed). Only confirm and back move, onto the game's A and B: a Switch Pro or Xbox controller with X and Y bound to its X and Y labels keeps them (0.5.0 swapped the game's X and Y on it in every menu and message: a lesson's 'Y' was its X), an Xbox controller's own bindings still give B on its B and X on its X in a menu, and with an audience member winding up a throw the battle menu's X stays on the field's X button
log_must: ^\[menulayer\] Xbox, its own bindings \(A bottom, B left, X right, Y top\): A->A B->X X->B Y->Y \(moved\)$
^\[menulayer\] Xbox, its own bindings, an audience member winding up a throw \(X kept\): A->A B->B X->X Y->Y \(as they are\)$
^\[menulayer\] PlayStation, its own bindings: A->A B->B X->X Y->Y \(as they are\)$
^\[menulayer\] Switch Pro, its own bindings \(by place: A bottom, B right\): A->B B->A X->X Y->Y \(moved\)$
^\[menulayer\] Switch Pro bound by its labels \(A right, B bottom, X top, Y left\): A->A B->B X->X Y->Y \(as they are\)$
^\[menulayer\] Xbox, Swap confirm and back: A->B B->X X->A Y->Y \(moved\)$
^\[menulayer\] Xbox, Y bound to its left button and X to its top \(B right\): A->A B->B X->X Y->Y \(as they are\)$
